tagline: Ninety miles of railroad grade with the rails taken up.
intro: The byway runs on the railroad itself, or on what is left of it, nearly 90 miles of Central Pacific grade built by hand in 1869 across the Great Salt Lake Desert, between the Nevada line and the country just west of Golden Spike. The rails came up in 1942. The earthworks and culverts stayed.

In 1904 the Lucin Cutoff carried the main line across the Great Salt Lake, and the towns along the old grade were left on a quiet branch. The BLM counts it as the longest stretch of original railroad grade remaining in the country, with more than 20 interpretive sites among the foundations.

moments.title: Terrace
moments.text: Once a division point with a 16-stall roundhouse and perhaps a thousand people, Terrace is down to a pile of red bricks and the outline of the turntable beside the grade.

moments.title: Matlin
moments.text: Chinese railroad workers built this section town in 1869, and what remains is the shape of a wye laid in 1900, still traced in the grade.

moments.title: Kelton
moments.text: Kelton once ran stages to Boise, and after the main line moved south the weekly local train on its stretch would often stop for a half-hour of rabbit hunting.

practical: There are no facilities or services along the byway, and flat tires are common on the rough grade. The BLM advises carrying plenty of water and spare tires.
